hazard: Lack of updated falls risk assessment and care plan

reports.title: Bridget Gormley: Prevention of future deaths report

promises.quote: Following this very sad incident we have made a number of changes to the provision of care and services at Latimer Court, and these have been adopted across the organisation in other services and divisions where appropriate
promises.summary: Implement monthly care plan reviews and audit by General Manager

promises.quote: At Barchester Healthcare, all residents care plans are reviewed by the senior carer in a residential home every month or when anything significant changes in their care or support requirements such as a fall
promises.summary: Monthly care plan reviews by senior carer

promises.quote: Following any fall or found on floor incident the falls risk assessment should be reviewed and the falls diary completed. The falls care plan should be updated accordingly and referrals made as appropriate
promises.summary: Review falls risk assessment after each fall

promises.quote: Barchester Healthcare have also now developed and introduced a specific Post Falls Assessment Tool to aid with the assessment of a resident following a fall or found on floor incident

As part of the lessons learnt as identified by the General Manager at Latimer Court it was highlighted that staff required further training from the organisation's Clinical Development Nurse in the approach to and completion of documentation

concerns.quote: During the course of her evidence, the inquest heard that Mrs. Gormley had suffered four falls at Latimer Court between 31 March 2022 and 4 April 2022, and a further four falls between 12 July 2022 and 17 July 2022. Latimer Court's registered home manager, [REDACTED], conceded in her evidence that neither Mrs. [name redacted] Risk Assessment document, nor her Falls Care plan document were updated following any of these falls, and that they should have been so updated
concerns.hazard: lack of updated falls risk assessment and care plan

concerns.quote: [REDACTED] was unable to explain why these important documents had not been updated as they should have been by staff at Latimer Court. There is therefore concern that staff at Latimer Court did not, and may still not understand their duties and responsibilities to update residents' documentation in such circumstances

reports.title: Keith Inseon: Prevention of Future Deaths Report

concerns.quote: the record keeping was inaccurate, contained gaps in the information, and engaged my duty under paragraph 7, Schedule 5, of the Coroners and Justice Act 2009 and regulations 28 and 29 of the Coroners (Investigations) Regulations 2013
Mr [name redacted] was at risk of suffering from falls and required an altered diet
Mr [name redacted] suffered a choking episode on food. Mr [name redacted] developed aspiration pneumonia and, despite treatment, Mr [name redacted] condition deteriorated and he died

links.explanation: Both reports highlight failures in documenting post‑fall information that should trigger further safety actions. The earlier case concerns missing updates to falls risk assessments and care plans; the later case concerns missing recording of observation scores after a fall.
links.earlier_quote: Latimer Court's registered home manager, [REDACTED], conceded in her evidence that neither Mrs. [name redacted] Risk Assessment document, nor her Falls Care plan document were updated following any of these falls
links.later_quote: It was noted in the evidence, that the observation scores taken for Mr [name redacted] following his fall had not all been recorded in Mr [name redacted] care notes.
